problem: Zero-shot LLM-based VLN agents delegate all navigation to the LLM, which understands real-world spatial layout poorly. They lag behind specialist VLN models and are very slow and costly. Fine-tuned LLM agents lose commonsense reasoning and lack VLN data.
motivation: Specialist models are efficient and accurate in routine cases but fail in unfamiliar situations (looping, myopic decisions, no error recovery). LLMs have commonsense and reasoning but are slow and lack spatial expertise. Inspired by dual-process theory, use the fast expert by default and call the LLM only when anomalies are detected.
key_idea: A dual-process VLN system in which a lightweight transformer expert (Runner) navigates normally and a Regulator detects anomalies (looping, GNN score, stop check) and hands control to a GPT-4o chain-of-thought Ruminator.
insight: Combining expert and LLM beats either alone. Removing the LLM drops REVERIE SPL from 42.14 to 36.47, while a weak LLM (MiniGPT-4, SPL 35.73) is worse than no LLM, so the Ruminator's benefit depends on the LLM's reasoning strength. Among Regulator criteria, the GNN scoring criterion matters most for navigation (w/o scoring: SR -2.05, SPL -2.76), and the ending check matters most for grounding (RGSPL -4.01). Sharing the memory bank helps (SPL -1.19 without it). Because the LLM is invoked only on anomalies, inference is about 5x faster than other LLM-assisted methods.
method: Runner: GridMM-style lightweight (~160M) transformer expert; takes RGB-D and pose, stores features in an egocentric grid memory, fuses them with instruction embeddings in a cross-modal encoder, and predicts actions with a 2-layer FFN.

Ruminator: GPT-4o with CoT prompting in three steps (perception into text descriptions, planning conditioned on the previous plan and history, prediction over listed candidate viewpoints); uses a structured text template (instruction, observation, trajectory, map, options) and shares the memory bank with the Runner; once triggered it takes over until the episode ends.
Regulator looping criterion: triggers the Ruminator when the max revisit count of any viewpoint exceeds τ_r=4 or trajectory length exceeds τ_l=20.

Regulator scoring criterion: a 2-layer graph attention GNN with edge encoding over the topological history map (node features: position, last visit time, visual embedding). It is trained self-supervised with pseudo-labels (0 if the trajectory succeeded or lies on the GT path, else 1) on train and val-seen trajectories; triggers if the output exceeds τ_g=0.35.
Regulator ending criterion: when the Runner predicts STOP, GPT-4o is asked with the instruction and the current panorama whether this is the destination; if not, the Ruminator takes over.

Critical formulation: after switching, GPT-4o judges from instruction, history and observation whether to restart from the start viewpoint (memory bank reset) and generates corrective planning, clearing misleading history.

setting.backbone: GridMM-based Runner (~160M, trained) + GPT-4o (frozen, Ruminator/Regulator) + small GNN scoring model (self-supervised)
setting.training_data: Runner trained on standard R2R/REVERIE data following the GridMM repo; GNN scorer trained on trajectories sampled from train and val-seen splits with algorithmic pseudo-labels; GPT-4o prompted, not tuned
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (adjacent navigable viewpoints, STOP)
setting.privileged: none (GT path used only to make pseudo-labels for the scorer on training splits)

numbers_note: R2R metrics are printed as integers in the paper's table (SR 77, SPL 66). The abstract's SPL/RGSPL gains (3.28/3.30) are relative to the best previous method (SUSA).
results: R3 reaches R2R val-unseen SR 77 / SPL 66 / NE 2.76 and REVERIE val-unseen SR 53.76 / SPL 42.14 / RGS 37.94 / RGSPL 29.86. It beats the strongest baselines (SUSA on REVERIE SPL 38.86, RGSPL 26.56; BEVBert/GridMM on R2R SR 75) by 3.28 SPL and 3.30 RGSPL on REVERIE. It also needs roughly one-fifth of the inference time of other LLM-assisted methods.
limitations: Still relies on the proprietary GPT-4o API for the Ruminator and Regulator checks (cost, latency on triggered steps), and quality depends on the LLM; a weak LLM hurts.

Only R2R and REVERIE in the discrete simulator, with no real-robot or continuous-environment evaluation; hyperparameters (τ_r, τ_l, τ_g) are hand-calibrated and the Ruminator takes over exclusively with no way back to the Runner.
The Runner and GNN scorer still require VLN-specific training, so the system is not fully zero-shot; the 'zero-shot' claim refers to LLM usage.
